title: ICSE Class-8 | Physics | Test | Matter | physical qwantitie and measurement
description: ICSE Class-8 | Physics | Test | Matter | physical qwantitie and measurement
subject: physics

questions.question: According to the kinetic theory of matter, which of the following statements are true? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Molecules are in a state of continuous random motion.
Intermolecular force of attraction is maximum in gases.
Kinetic energy of molecules increases with an increase in temperature.
Matter is composed of very small particles called molecules.

questions.explanation: The kinetic theory states that particles are tiny, always moving, and their speed depends on temperature. Gases actually have the minimum intermolecular force.

questions.question: A block of wood has a mass of $120\text{ g}$ and a volume of $150\text{ cm}^3$. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density is calculated as $\text{Mass} / \text{Volume} = 120 / 150 = 0.8\text{ g/cm}^3$.

questions.question: Which of the following processes involve the absorption of heat energy? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Sublimation and vaporization are endothermic processes, meaning they require heat to break intermolecular bonds.

questions.question: The relative density of a substance is $7.8$. What is its density in SI units?
questions.explanation: Thus, $7.8 \times 1000 = 7800\text{ kg/m}^3$.

questions.question: Which factors increase the rate of evaporation of a liquid? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a surface phenomenon; larger surface area, higher temperature, and wind speed all accelerate the process, while humidity slows it down.

questions.question: Why does an iron nail sink in water but an iron ship floats?

options.text: The nail is heavier than the ship.
The ship displaces a weight of water equal to its own weight.
The density of iron changes when it is shaped into a ship.
The ship contains a lot of air which increases its average density.

questions.explanation: According to the Law of Flotation, a body floats if it displaces water equal to its own weight. The hollow shape of the ship increases volume, reducing average density.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of the solid state? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Solids are rigid and incompressible due to very strong intermolecular forces and fixed molecular positions.

questions.question: A density bottle weighs $30\text{ g}$ when empty, $55\text{ g}$ when filled with water, and $50\text{ g}$ when filled with an unknown oil. Calculate the Relative Density (RD) of the oil.
questions.explanation: $\text{Mass of water} = 55 - 30 = 25\text{ g}$; $\text{Mass of oil} = 50 - 30 = 20\text{ g}$. $\text{RD} = \text{Mass of oil} / \text{Mass of equal volume of water} = 20 / 25 = 0.8$.

questions.question: What happens to the intermolecular space when a substance is cooled?
questions.explanation: Cooling reduces the kinetic energy of molecules, bringing them closer together and decreasing the intermolecular space.

questions.question: Identify the substances that undergo sublimation. (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Camphor, Iodine, and Dry Ice (solid carbon dioxide) transition directly from solid to gas upon heating.

questions.question: An object of density $1.2\text{ g/cm}^3$ is dropped into a liquid of density $1.5\text{ g/cm}^3$. The object will:
questions.explanation: Since the object's density is less than the liquid's density, it will float according to the principle of flotation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Brownian motion are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is the zig-zag motion of particles.
It is only observed in solids.
It proves that molecules are in constant motion.
It increases with an increase in temperature.

questions.explanation: Brownian motion is observed in fluids (liquids and gases) and is driven by molecular collisions.

questions.question: The density of mercury is $13600\text{ kg/m}^3$. Its density in $\text{g/cm}^3$ is:
questions.explanation: To convert $\text{kg/m}^3$ to $\text{g/cm}^3$, divide by $1000$. $13600 / 1000 = 13.6$.

questions.question: During the change of state from solid to liquid, the temperature:
questions.explanation: During melting, the heat supplied (latent heat) is used to overcome intermolecular forces, so the temperature does not rise until the transition is complete.

questions.question: Which instruments can be used to measure the volume of an irregular solid? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: A measuring cylinder and Eureka can are used for volume displacement; a balance measures mass, and a hydrometer measures density.

questions.question: A stone of mass $75\text{ g}$ is lowered into a measuring cylinder containing water. The water level rises from $25\text{ ml}$ to $40\text{ ml}$. The density of the stone is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Volume} = 40 - 25 = 15\text{ ml}$ (or $15\text{ cm}^3$). $\text{Density} = 75 / 15 = 5\text{ g/cm}^3$.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for gases? (Select all that apply)

options.text: They have no definite shape or volume.
They exert pressure in all directions.

questions.explanation: Gases have large intermolecular spaces, allowing them to be compressed and to fill any container entirely.

questions.question: What is the unit of Relative Density?
questions.explanation: Relative density is a ratio of two similar quantities (densities), so the units cancel out.

questions.question: Cohesive force is the force of attraction between:
questions.explanation: Cohesion occurs between like molecules (e.g., water-water), while adhesion occurs between different molecules (e.g., water-glass).

questions.question: When a solid is converted directly into gas, the process is called:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct transition from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase.

questions.question: A body floats in a liquid with $1/3$rd of its volume outside the liquid. If the density of the liquid is $1200\text{ kg/m}^3$, the density of the body is:
questions.explanation: Submerged volume is $2/3$. $\text{Density of body} = (\text{Submerged Fraction}) \times \text{Density of liquid} = (2/3) \times 1200 = 800\text{ kg/m}^3$.

questions.question: Which properties are characteristic of the liquid state? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Definite volume but no definite shape.

questions.explanation: Liquids take the shape of their container but maintain a constant volume and have significant fluidity.

questions.question: Boiling is a ________ phenomenon, whereas evaporation is a ________ phenomenon.
questions.explanation: Boiling occurs throughout the mass of the liquid (bulk), while evaporation only happens at the top layer (surface).

questions.question: A cube of side $2\text{ cm}$ has a mass of $16\text{ g}$. Its density is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Volume} = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8\text{ cm}^3$. $\text{Density} = 16 / 8 = 2\text{ g/cm}^3$.

questions.question: Why does ice float on water?

options.text: Density of ice is less than density of water.
Ice is a solid and water is a liquid.
Ice traps air bubbles that make it heavier.
The temperature of ice is lower.

questions.explanation: Water expands upon freezing, meaning a fixed mass of ice occupies more volume than water, making it less dense.

questions.question: Which of the following increase the pressure exerted by a gas? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Decreasing the volume of the container.
Increasing the volume of the container.

questions.explanation: Pressure increases when molecular collisions with the walls increase, which happens with more heat, more molecules, or less space.

questions.question: The ratio of the mass of a certain volume of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water at $4^\circ\text{C}$ is known as:
questions.explanation: This is the formal definition of Relative Density.

questions.question: If the density of an object is exactly equal to the density of the liquid it is placed in, the object will:

options.text: Float completely submerged at any depth.

questions.explanation: This is neutral buoyancy; the upthrust exactly balances the weight while the object is fully under the surface.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of "Matter"? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Matter must have mass and occupy space. Light is energy and does not have rest mass or volume.

questions.question: A piece of metal of mass $50\text{ g}$ has an RD of $2.5$. Its volume is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Density} = \text{RD} \times 1\text{ g/cm}^3 = 2.5\text{ g/cm}^3$. $\text{Volume} = \text{Mass} / \text{Density} = 50 / 2.5 = 20\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.question: In which state of matter is the kinetic energy of molecules highest?
questions.explanation: Molecules in gases move at high speeds in all directions, possessing maximum kinetic energy compared to solids or liquids.

questions.question: The process of a gas changing into a liquid is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when gas particles lose energy and come closer to form a liquid.

questions.question: Which of the following applies to the "Plimsoll Line" on ships? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It indicates the maximum depth to which a ship can be safely submerged.
It varies based on the density of the water (Salt vs Fresh).
It indicates the speed of the ship.

questions.explanation: Plimsoll lines are safety marks reflecting how density differences in different seas affect buoyancy.

questions.question: A density bottle is used to find the density of:
questions.explanation: A density bottle is designed to hold a precise volume of liquid or a mix of liquid and solid powder to determine density.

questions.question: The force that opposes the downward weight of an object in a fluid is:
questions.explanation: Upthrust (or Buoyant force) acts vertically upwards on any object immersed in a fluid.

questions.question: Which of the following happens when a solid melts? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Melting involves breaking the rigid structure of a solid, which increases space and potential energy while temperature stays constant at the melting point.

questions.question: A body of mass $200\text{ g}$ weighs $160\text{ g}$ in water. The upthrust acting on it is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Upthrust} = \text{Weight in Air} - \text{Weight in Water} = 200 - 160 = 40\text{ gf}$.

questions.question: Deposition is the process where:
questions.explanation: Deposition (or desublimation) is the reverse of sublimation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about mass are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is the quantity of matter contained in a body.
It changes from place to place.
It is measured using a beam balance.

questions.explanation: Mass is constant regardless of location; weight is what changes based on gravity.

questions.question: An empty density bottle weighs $22\text{ g}$. When full of water, it weighs $47\text{ g}$. The volume of the bottle is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Mass of water} = 47 - 22 = 25\text{ g}$. Since density of water is $1\text{ g/cm}^3$, volume is $25\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.question: Why do we feel cold when we apply perfume or alcohol on our skin?

options.text: It evaporates quickly taking heat from our skin.
It reacts chemically with the skin.
It blocks the pores of the skin.

questions.explanation: This is "evaporative cooling." Volatile liquids use the body's heat to change state into vapor.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for an object that sinks in water?
questions.explanation: Sinking occurs when the downward force of gravity (weight) exceeds the maximum upward buoyant force.

questions.question: Which of the following are fluids? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: A fluid is any substance that can flow, which includes all liquids and gases.

questions.question: A hydrometer works on the principle of:
questions.explanation: A hydrometer floats at different levels based on the density of the liquid, displacing its own weight of the liquid (Archimedes' principle).

questions.question: Surface tension in liquids is caused by:
questions.explanation: Cohesive forces between liquid molecules pull them together, creating a "skin" or tension on the surface.

questions.question: If the volume of a given mass of gas is doubled at constant temperature, the density becomes:
questions.explanation: $\text{Density} = \text{Mass} / \text{Volume}$. If Volume is doubled ($2V$), density becomes $M / 2V$, which is half the original.

questions.question: Which of the following are units of volume? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Litre, cubic centimetre, and cubic metre all measure space/volume. $\text{kg/m}^3$ is a unit of density.

questions.question: A balloon filled with Hydrogen rises in the air because:

options.text: Weight of air displaced is more than the weight of the balloon.
Hydrogen is a very heavy gas.
The balloon is attracted by the sun.
Gravity does not act on Hydrogen.

questions.explanation: The upthrust from the surrounding air is greater than the total weight of the balloon and the light hydrogen inside.

questions.question: What is the density of water at $4^\circ\text{C}$ in SI units?
questions.explanation: Water has its maximum density at $4^\circ\text{C}$, which is $1000\text{ kg/m}^3$.

questions.question: Which of these is an application of the Law of Flotation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A car moving on a road.

questions.explanation: Submarines, life jackets, and balloons all manipulate density and displacement to control buoyancy and flotation.
